subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-container-creation hook for dynamic sandbox bind mounts

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted pre-container sandbox policy seam for per-session bind mounts, and if so should it be core config, plugin SDK API, or another sandbox-policy layer?
rationale: The request changes who can decide host filesystem exposure before container creation and introduces possible host-side execution/config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the trust and API boundary.

options.title: Design a sandbox policy seam
options.body: Keep the issue open and have a sandbox/security owner define a narrow pre-container policy contract before any implementation PR.

options.title: Limit to static binds
options.body: Reject dynamic per-session bind mounts for now and keep operators on explicit agent configs plus existing static bind validation.

options.title: Move toward plugin SDK only
options.body: Treat this as a plugin API extension request and avoid adding a core `resolveBinds` executable config field.

recommendation.title: Design a sandbox policy seam
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and have a sandbox/security owner define a narrow pre-container policy contract before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the central sandbox bind precedence and validation history in this area traces to steipete-authored commits.
